newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy "Euro Tax" to raise 10-12 trln lire - source.
newsitem.headline: Italy "Euro Tax" to raise 10-12 trln lire - source.

text.p: The special "Europe tax", which the Treasury plans to introduce to improve Italy's chances of being a founder member of the single European currency, will raise between 10-12 trillion lire in 1997, a government source said.

The source added that two trillion lire of savings would come from a "rationalisation" of pensions spending and a further two trillion lire from health savings, although there would be no new hospital treatment charges.

The "Euro Tax" is expected to be a special one-off measure to help Italy cut its deficit to gross domestic product ratio to three percent in 1997, the magic figure countries must meet to stand a chance of joining planned European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the start in 1999.
Corriere della Sera newspaper on Thursday said it would be levied in the form of a once-off increase in income tax.
The full budget package will be presented on Friday following a cabinet meeting. Parliament has until the end of the year to pass the bill into law. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
